newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-QNI forms nickel mine joint venture.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-QNI forms nickel mine joint venture.

text.p: QNI Ltd said on Thursday it will form a joint venture to mine lateritic nickel ore in New Caledonia.

QNI said it will hold a 67 percent interest in the joint venture through its wholly-owned subsidiary QNI Nouvelle Caledonia, with mining group Societe des Mines de la Tontouta (SMT) of New Caledonia owning the remaining 33 percent.
The joint venture company will be called Societe des Mines de Bogota and will acquire 40 existing SMT Bogota Peninsula mining tenements for A$35 million to be paid over 15 years, QNI said.
A further A$40 million would be spent developing the deposits, QNI said.
QNI said it has agreed to provide funding for the project, which could be met from cash flow and existing loan facilities.
The venture would be the first direct investment by QNI in a development project in New Caledonia, managing director Wyn Davies said in a statement.
The project was part of a long-term strategy to secure dedicated ore supplies while continuing the policy of diversifying ore supplies, he said.
It was expected that about one million wet tonnes of limonitic ore would be supplied from the Bogota deposits to the refinery. The project is scheduled to start in late 1996 or early 1997.
